prepared offline for the original 50mm f/1.4 profile. Its protocol/controller/
main/driver C files remain upstream; it uses a separate reproducible builder.
AF 3.0 remains held after capture/shutdown failure. See [the baseline evidence](../docs/evidence/upstream-baseline-2026-10-14.md).

Current source builds **AF 3.0** under `ea9/build/arbitrated`, with camera BCD
0x30 and loader 3.0.0. `em_arbitration` separates capture/RX/TX/session/shutdown

Dependency versions, official source URLs and digests are pinned in

the pinned released templates and the new candidate and a digest pin; it personalizes only the
reserved profile row. A template with its zeroed profile is intentionally invalid.

Changes from the reference:

- The frozen metadata release uses a dedicated `metadata_main.c` entry point; the motion implementation is not

- `lens_profile.c` validates the versioned CRC-protected profile and applies

# Device workflow: prototype 0.15.0, build 19

Open `dist/Open LM-EA9.app`. The **Device** tab shows the adapter photo,
connection, dated firmware read and the last USB-verified lens setting.
Actual aperture is **Unknown**; the displayed fixed f-number is camera metadata.
Use the lens ring to stop down. The library editor lets you override the fixed
camera f-number while retaining the unknown physical setting.
The secondary **Lens Library** tab retains the photographs and metadata editor.

Startup diagnostic **3.2.0** was uploaded for the original 50mm f/1.4
profile on October 15; physical reconnect and strict byte verification are pending.
See [the installation record](evidence/upstream-32-upload-2026-10-15.md). USB tools provide a separate **Install Startup Diagnostic 3.2.0**
action; changing the dropdown does not install it. Other/edited profiles are
rejected. The native CLI equivalents are `prepare-startup` and `apply-startup`.
This upload followed a separately coordinated owner request. Installed 3.2 routes
the main action to USB tools, labels camera compatibility unqualified and avoids
repeat installation. After one coordinated camera cycle, save a read-only backup
and use the offline decoder, as described in [the diagnostic runbook](upstream-startup-diagnostic-test.md).
Initial full-image verification includes the blank log area. Later log retrieval
does not relax that check; ordinary image inspection still rejects changed bytes.

## Change a lens

1. Connect the adapter through its USB cap with TECHART Update closed.
2. Choose a lens in the **Lens profile** dropdown on Device. All eight requested
   lenses are included, with the corrected Biotar 58mm f/2. The selected-on-Mac
   preview shows the focal length and reported aperture that will be applied.
3. Confirm **Updater closed · USB cap reconnected**, then click **Apply profile**.
4. After upload, physically unplug and reconnect the cap. The app detects the
   new connection; confirm the prerequisite again and click **Verify lens**.
5. Use the adapter on the camera after byte verification succeeds.

Choosing a profile saves only a local preparation. The on-adapter photo and
setting retain the last verified value until the uploaded image is verified.
An unchanged profile shows **Up to date**. The primary action preserves the
verified installed firmware variant, including legacy AF 2.1. Upgrading to the
upstream 3.1 baseline was a separate **USB tools → Experimental autofocus** action,
compiled only for the original Contax Zeiss 50mm f/1.4 profile. It does not use
a runtime lens-profile row. Other/edited profiles are rejected before USB.
When that baseline is installed, the dropdown explains its fixed configuration
and offers USB tools rather than pretending another profile can be applied.
The CLI `apply-upstream` still selects held 3.1 for explicit recovery/research;
do not retry it for camera use. Historical `apply-af` still selects held 3.0.
Plain `apply` selects metadata-only 2.0.

The app checks macOS USB/HID descriptors and bounded local history every two
seconds, on launch, and when it becomes active. It detects connection changes
and reloads CLI-published verification records while the window stays open.
The monitor cancels when the view ends, skips active operations and rejects
overlapping refreshes. A changed registry ID, blocked connection or discovery
failure clears the connection acknowledgement. Multiple adapters disable USB
operations. Discovery failure clears the displayed device list.

Automatic refresh sends **no HID feature reports, CHECK, READ or START**.
Firmware and lens labels remain dated local evidence associated with the
qualified unit's serial, not fresh USB readings or identification of a passive
mounted lens. **Read Version** and **Read Adapter Lens** remain explicit in
USB tools. This distinction matters because an armed stock bootloader can
interpret an ordinary read request as the next firmware page. Keep the physical
reconnect guard even though discovery itself is automatic.

The main view uses the existing sourced photos, compact adapter/firmware card,
verified lens photo and a visible dropdown/apply row. No new remote images or
runtime network requests were added. The earlier visual release was built and inspected with
the connected adapter; 0.14 packaging and tests were offline. Its last saved 2.1.0/50mm f/1.4 history loaded correctly;

> Current app: **0.14.0, build 17** shows actual aperture as Unknown separately
> from the fixed camera f-number and packages the direct upstream 3.1 baseline.
> The baseline is fixed to the original 50mm f/1.4 profile and is prepared offline.
> See [its provenance and validation](evidence/upstream-baseline-2026-10-14.md).
> Automatic refresh, the Device dropdown and firmware-preserving lens changes
> remain. AF 3.0 upload and strict reconnect verification passed on October 14;

> [AF 3.0 milestone](evidence/af-30-candidate-2026-10-13.md).

# macOS prototype

> Current follow-up (prototype 0.3.0): the [USB metadata milestone](usb-metadata-milestone.md) adds a reviewed, bounded application upload, mandatory physical reconnect and full byte verification. Its first firmware candidate uses the reference C implementation with motor motion disabled. [Actual measurements](evidence/usb-metadata-milestone-2026-10-10.md) distinguish stock upload qualification, custom read-back and pending camera checks. The material below records the earlier research/prototype stage.

Version 0.2.0, October 10, 2026. Implements the user's authorized next step:

After an uncertain exchange, cancellation, crash or interrupted session,
physically reconnect and refresh. The connection's registry ID is persisted in
`usb-reconnect-required.json` before the transaction and cleared on successful
completion. Relaunching the app does not bypass this guard. Conservative open
failures may also require reconnect. There are no automatic transport retries.
Refresh is manual; the prototype does not provide live hotplug notifications.

The package includes device serial/unit data. It is private local evidence,
with a `0700` directory and `0600` files. The app sends nothing to a server.
Complete flash read-back is verified; restoring an adapter from the backup is
**not qualified**. Other factory auxiliary rows and unique-ID words are outside
this backup. No install, restore, arbitrary memory access, feature report,
reset, motor command or profile-apply action exists in the app.

## Command-line diagnostics

The packaged CLI uses the same DeviceKit pipeline as the GUI:

```sh
./dist/ea9ctl inventory
./dist/ea9ctl backup /path/to/new-backup.ea9backup --idle
```

`--idle` acknowledges the same closed-updater/physical-reconnect prerequisite.
Inventory prints a redacted summary and sends no reports. Backup prints only
the destination, size, flash digest and exchange count. The manifest retains
private identity. `--state-directory PATH` can isolate the persistent reconnect
guard for development; use the shared default in normal operation. Run only
one USB client at a time.

# 3.6.0 — upstream C startup handoff, Contax Zeiss 50mm f/1.4

**Prepared offline; not uploaded or camera-qualified.** This extends frozen
[3.5](../3.5.0/README.md) with a scoped startup receive-ownership fix.
It retains the upstream controller, gains, optical tables, aperture policy,
motor/sensor drivers, wait budgets and diagnostic storage.

App **0.19.0/build 23** offers **USB tools → Install Upstream AF 3.6.0**.
Explicit commands: `prepare-handoff-upstream` / `apply-handoff-upstream`.
Earlier commands retain their images. Only the original unedited 50mm profile
is supported. Actual iris stays Unknown; factory reconstruction remains partial.

The pending uploaded 3.2 transaction still requires owner-confirmed physical
reconnect and strict full-image/protected-data verification. This offline
candidate does not resolve it or authorize another flash. See the
[future coordinated procedure](../../../docs/upstream-handoff-test.md),
[build/test workbench](../../upstream-hardening/next36/README.md),
[manifest](contax-zeiss-50-f1-4.manifest.json) and
[complete delta from 3.5](from-35.patch). Prior releases and stock recovery remain exact.

# Upstream AF 3.6 — future installation and camera acceptance

**Prepared offline only. No camera action is requested by this document.**
The [candidate](../firmware/candidates/3.6.0/README.md) and
[offline validation](evidence/upstream-36-handoff-2026-10-15.md) do not establish
A7C II stability. The current 3.2 upload still awaits owner-confirmed physical
reconnect and strict verification; resolve that existing transaction through its
normal guarded path before attempting a separate authorized 3.6 installation.
Never delete/edit the pending journal or reconnect marker to bypass it.

## Separate upload and byte verification

After explicit authorization, confirm the adapter is on the USB cap, the
TECHART updater is closed and the saved original profile is the unedited
Contax Zeiss 50mm f/1.4. App 0.19/build 23 exposes **USB tools → Install Upstream AF 3.6.0**. Its CLI equivalent, for that future coordinated operation:

```sh
dist/ea9ctl apply-handoff-upstream contax-zeiss-50-f1-4 --idle
# Stop. Owner must physically unplug/reconnect and confirm the new connection.
# Keep the adapter off the camera until strict verification has passed.
dist/ea9ctl verify --idle
```

The fresh same-unit two-pass backup, durable journal and protected data checks
remain mandatory. START arms the connection: no CHECK/READ/control/end marker or
retry is sent afterward on that connection. An acknowledgement is not byte
verification. Require the complete 20,480-byte pristine image, including all
blank log pages, and existing protected metadata/flash/auxiliary checks. The
six established loader scratch bytes remain the sole metadata exception.
Record an independent offline comparison of the verification backup before
camera use. A decoder prefix match cannot substitute for this gate.

## One initial loaded-lens cycle

After the strict gate succeeds, coordinate one cycle before AF-S. With the
A7C II off and camera USB disconnected, mount the LM-EA9, C/Y-to-M converter and
50mm lens. Set the physical focus ring to infinity and iris to f/1.4. Select
still-photo A, EV0, Auto ISO, **Manual Focus separately in Focus → AF/MF → Focus
Mode**, and Pre-AF Off where available. Record actual settings; unknown settings
stay unknown. The A exposure dial alone does not select MF.

1. Switch on without shutter/AF-ON. Note preview updating/brightness, aperture
   display (nominal f/1.4), motor movement/sound and whether it stops.
2. If responsive and quiet, wait ten seconds after movement stops. If the preview
   freezes or aperture stays `--`, skip photo/AF and switch off once.
3. Only if preview, aperture and motion are normal and MF is confirmed, take one
   photograph. Record whether it saves and its exposure; preserve its local path
   for optional EXIF inspection. Switch off once and leave it off.

For a freeze, shutdown nonresponse, grinding, repeated stop impacts or abnormal
continuous drive for about two seconds, stop: switch off; remove the battery if
unresponsive or motion continues; do not retry or restart for missing details.
Report the exact trigger (startup/half/full press), saved-photo status and
shutdown behavior. No further camera cycle or AF-S is needed before log review.

This candidate intentionally starts no new parking drive on shutdown. Motor
silence is not proof of AF failure or physical infinity. Physical iris remains
manual and Unknown to the adapter; the nominal f-number cannot track ring changes.
Do not introduce exposure offsets based only on a mismatched f-number report.

## Read-only logs and next AF-S decision

With the camera off/unpowered and motor stopped, return to the USB cap and
physically reconnect, updater closed. Confirm that state before a new read-only
native backup. Use new private paths:

```sh
dist/ea9ctl backup /new/after-36.ea9backup --idle
python3 scripts/decode-startup-diagnostics.py /new/after-36.ea9backup --output /new/after-36.json
```

Trace v2 persists only on terminal shutdown after UART disable, or terminal
fail-stop. The ten-second idle does **not** flush 3.6. Battery removal, full/torn
storage or an unentered terminal path can leave blank/incomplete logs. First 24
and latest 24 RAM retention is bounded; a summary reports planned events, while
the decoder reports how many survived. A shutdown marker proves reaching that
software point, not electrical power removal or a successful next boot.

Decoder identity checks require the exact version, complete published image and manifest
pins, immutable prefix, and per-page structure/CRC; a native manifest also needs
two flash/auxiliary reads and the full flash hash. It explicitly does not verify
installation. Page `state: valid` means structure/CRC only; `recordTrust` and cohort checks separately identify inconsistent, partial or unassociated evidence. CRC is not authentication. Camera-written diagnostic pages mean ordinary `inspect` no longer
recognizes a pristine image; use `backup` plus the decoder after camera use.
Compare all outside-log flash and auxiliary data separately. Do not erase/reset
logs; raw unit dumps and actual camera exchanges stay private.

Only after a successful preview/MF-capture/idle/shutdown cycle and log review,
plan a separate bounded AF-S comparison with actual AF-S and Pre-AF Off settings,
a bright stationary target, infinity focus-ring position and physical f/1.4.
Record lock/release, hunting, motion and saved-photo sharpness. Neither a green
indicator nor host tests qualify optical accuracy. AF-C/video, zoom changes,
other lenses and factory parity remain later acceptance work.

The builder requires exact pinned 3.5 materialization at
`artifacts/private/absolute35a`. If absent, reproduce the
[3.5 prerequisites](../next35/README.md) first:

```sh

```

```sh
scripts/swift-local.sh test

```
